scope.product: Offline research-expert discovery over a dated, sourced context graph
scope.architecture: Python core and FastAPI; SQLite graph and sessions; local lexical/vector indexes; React and TypeScript client through API only
scope.time_budget_policy: No deadline or hour cap supplied; complete phases in order and report measured work in chat.
intentional_exclusions: Redis and a separate graph database for the local submission
scope.production_targets_policy: Discuss in the final design; do not claim measured capacity without a corresponding benchmark.

acceptance.expected: Versioned API/batch contracts, architecture choice, acceptance criteria, and fixed experiment configuration exist.
Offline streaming XML/gzip handles DBLP publication types, entities, encodings, nested titles, missing metadata and suffixed identities.
At least 50000 real DBLP papers ingested with source checksum, timing, throughput, Python allocation peak and process RSS.
Repeated ingestion preserves graph records; source corrections replace relationships; malformed input rolls back atomically with a failed audit record.
Graph has only known-year pre-cutoff papers, historical author labels and historical venues. Train, validation and test queries are disjoint later periods; repeated titles are excluded.
Future paper titles produce automatic authorship labels; manifests report newcomer coverage and label limitations.
Seeded per-authorship name corruption uses historical context, removes disambiguation suffixes, and stores identity labels separately from observations.
Fixed source/config reproduces slice, query labels and noise bytes; every artifact has a digest and experiments cannot silently overwrite previous runs.
Blocked matcher uses names, coauthors, venues and years; report candidate recall and precision/recall with incorrect merge and split tests.
Idempotent author-paper, author-venue and coauthorship edges have typed endpoints, dates, sources and clear error costs.
Lexical and off-the-shelf semantic dense baselines plus hybrid candidate retrieval run offline.
Train a model on separate labels, compare against baselines, report ablations, and address a documented hard case.
LLM structured topics/recency are schema validated with an offline fallback.
Claims cite evidence; automatic verification reports unsupported-claim rate.
At least three schema-validated graph tools, multi-turn shortlist/reject memory, visible memory application and deletion.
Query/title injections cannot trigger tools as instructions; at least six scripted scenarios report success and injection resistance.
Search supports loading, empty, error and stale-request cancellation states.
Results expose score, explanation, expandable evidence and unsupported claims; profiles expose sourced publication timelines and topics.
Assistant panel shows calls and applied memory; shortlist/reject remain correct after failed requests.
Safe rendering, keyboard navigation, accessible labels, component tests and search-assistant-shortlist end-to-end test.
Required ./run handles an unseen XML slice offline with scores, explanations, papers, years and collaborators.
Health endpoint, logs, Compose application, exact setup in five commands or fewer, offline tests and CI.
Measured nDCG@10/MRR, baselines, ablation, leakage audit, controlled fairness check and two significant failure analyses.
2-3 page design with scaling/privacy, measured results with commands, AI-use statement, 3-5 minute recording and clean offline startup.

non_negotiable: No API keys or network required for runtime/tests
No secrets or raw DBLP in submission
External API spend below approximately USD 5
